response_text: In round-robin scheduling, using a queue to store TCBs instead of an array allows threads to be managed more simply. In a queue, the currently running thread is always at the front. When a thread yields, it is removed from the front of the queue and placed at the back, and then the next thread is scheduled to run. This method eliminates the need for index tracking, which would be required in arrays. It simplifies the logic of rotating between threads in multithreading. Furthermore, queues are easier to extend in more advanced systems where they may need to be dynamically allocated or removed. While using an array is sufficient and simpler for smaller systems like in this lab, a queue structure is better as it offers more flexibility and maintenance.\n
